title: Why Everything Depends on Setting the Right Priorities
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece makes the case that prioritization, more than any other single skill, determines a leader's daily and long-term effectiveness. It argues that priorities are inherently short-lived and situational, and that leaders who fail to keep the list small end up with no real priorities at all. The author frames a large priority list as self-defeating, and recommends leaders continually interrogate whether their current task is genuinely the most important use of their time. The piece closes on a quote from author Brian Tracy about the outsized impact of choosing and completing the single most important task.
points: Priorities are short-lived and situational, not a fixed 'day job'.
A large list of priorities is functionally the same as having no priorities at all.
Lower items on a priority list aren't neglected, they simply wait their turn.
Letting others set your priorities by consuming your time and energy is framed as a failure of leadership discipline.
quotes: Priorities force people to focus on those things that matter most right now.
Priorities are never the leader’s “day job” or what they are expected to do. Instead, they are the highest and best use of time right now.
Ironically, having a large list of priorities actually equates to not having any at all.
Good leaders continually ask themselves this question: How important is what I’m doing if what I’m doing isn’t the most important thing?

Your ability to select your most important task at each moment, and then to get started on that task and to get it done both quickly and well, will probably have more of an impact on your success than any other quality or skill you can develop.
